summary: The husband brings a special mincha offering for his wife. It is different from all other menachos: it starts in a plain basket, has no oil or levonah, and is made of barley flour.

summary: The husband cannot add to her oath things from before she married him or after a divorce. The rule: he can only add things that would make her forbidden to him.

chunks.en: All agree that he does not add to her oath
chunks.st: All agree that he may stipulate with her through this oath

chunks.en: about the time before she was engaged to him, nor
chunks.st: neither with regard to what she did before becoming be-trothed to him,

chunks.en: about the time after she is divorced.
chunks.st: nor with regard to what she will do after she becomes divorced
chunks.stMore: from him. Similarly, if a husband divorced his wife, and while divorced

chunks.he: נִסְתְּרָה לְאַחֵר וְנִטְמֵאת וְאַחַר כָּךְ הֶחֱזִירָהּ,
chunks.en: If (while divorced) she was alone with another man and became tamei, and then he took her back,
chunks.st: she secluded herself with another man and became defiled, and afterward her husband took her back
chunks.stMore: and remarried her, and he then warned her about a specific man, and she secluded herself, and she is now about to drink the water of the sota,

chunks.en: he could not add that to her oath.
chunks.st: he cannot stipulate with her
chunks.stMore: that she take an oath that she did not become defiled during the period in which she was divorced. This is because her husband would become forbidden to her only if she had married another man after being divorced, not if she merely committed an act of promiscuity.

chunks.en: This is the rule:
chunks.st: This is the principle:

chunks.he: כֹּל שֶׁתִּבָּעֵל וְלֹא הָיְתָה אֲסוּרָה לוֹ,
chunks.en: Anything she did that would not make her forbidden to him,
chunks.st: In every case where if she would engage in sexual intercourse with someone else she would not become forbidden to her husband due to this act,

chunks.en: he does not add to her oath.
chunks.st: he may not stipulate with her
chunks.stMore: that her oath include that act. The oath can include only cases in which she would be rendered forbidden to him.
